title: Croniq trigger (producer) conformance case
description: Schema for a single language-agnostic conformance case that exercises a trigger (producer) client — `POST /v1/trigger`. Distinct from case-schema.json (the runner/consumer loop): a producer case makes explicit `trigger(...)` calls instead of running a poll loop, so it declares `trigger_config` + `trigger_calls` where a runner case declares `runner_config` + `handlers`. Kept in cases-trigger/ (not cases/) so runner bindings that enumerate cases/ keep passing untouched until they wire a trigger runner.

trigger_config.description: Maps to the trigger client's options object. `server_url` is NOT listed here — the binding injects the mock server's base URL, exactly as runner cases omit it from runner_config. The trigger client authenticates with ITS OWN credentials (jobs:trigger scope), independent of any runner.

trigger_calls.description: Ordered list of trigger(...) invocations the binding must make against the configured client, in order. Each call's server response comes from server_script (sequenced via match_count when a case fires the same endpoint more than once).

request.description: Arguments passed to the trigger client. Fields absent here MUST NOT appear in the outbound JSON body — assert their omission with expectations.http[].body_absent.

expect.description: The outcome the client must surface to the caller. Exactly one of `response` (call succeeds) or `error: true` (call raises/returns an error) by convention.

response.description: Subset match on the parsed TriggerResponse the client returns. Only listed fields are asserted. execution_id accepts '*' for any non-empty value.

error.description: true → the client MUST surface the call as an error (thrown exception / rejected future / err return), not a value.

on.description: HTTP method and path pattern. Path may include {param} placeholders.

match_count.description: If set, this rule only applies to the Nth-occurring match (1-based). Otherwise the rule is the fallthrough for all matches.

headers.description: Subset match on request headers (case-insensitive name, exact value or '*').

body_match.description: Subset match on the request JSON body. '*' wildcards any non-empty value.

body_absent.description: Top-level request-body keys that MUST NOT be present. Pins omission of unset optionals (a producer must not emit metadata/require/prefer/timeout/idempotency_key it was not given). Asserted against the first matching request.
